title: 스타듀 밸리
prompt:
INPUT: the attached image is the approved character; keep her.

CHARACTER: the same woman as the attached image — the personification of the game «스타듀 밸리» (simulation). Keep her face, eye and hair colors, haircut, skin tone and body proportions; expression and hair motion may change.

NOT ITS CHARACTERS: an original woman who is the game itself — no face or body of its hero, mascot, characters or creatures (she may wear their outfits); no title logo, box art, real brands, HUD overlay or readable text and numbers. Its items, places, colors, gear and interface shapes may appear recognizably.

NEVER DRAW for this game: "마을 주민(애비게일·세바스찬 등)의 얼굴"; "주니모·몬스터의 얼굴과 몸"; "로고·타이틀 글자"; "화면 위 시계·가방 칸 HUD"; "읽히는 글자·숫자".

STYLE: Glossy Korean mobile-game character art with an elegant anime face, smooth dimensional shading, luminous color accents and refined fabric and accessory rendering. Keep highlights selective and the figure sharply readable.

SIGNATURE (this one only, as an accessory or an object in the scene — never printed on or woven into the clothes): "나무 출하 상자와 파스닙 밭".

AGE: keep her age as in the attached image; add no wrinkles, folds or under-eye shadows, even when she smiles.

OUTPUT: one standalone off-duty scene of her in the outfit chosen in SCENE; her game shows only through accessories and objects around her — never in the outfit's colours, patterns or cut, never her form costume, its characters or logo. Era, place, activity, outfit, pose and camera follow SCENE (chosen).

FRAME: a vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) image. Compose the image for this frame; the Framing in SCENE sets how much of her shows.

WORLD: this scene happens inside the world of «스타듀 밸리», as if she simply lives there — a cozy pixel-art farming valley of crop fields, a seaside town square, glittering mines and a red barn at sunset. Its architecture, props, light and weather show the world; no characters, creatures, logos, on-screen graphics or interface.

SCENE (chosen):
Place: her own room in a building of her game's world
Activity: tying her hair up in front of a mirror
Outfit: a thin-strap camisole with wrap shorts tied at the hip
Pose: Stand at ease with relaxed shoulders and naturally balanced feet.
Orientation: rear three-quarter view with natural costume depth and occlusion; the head turns no more than a quarter turn, face in profile or three-quarter
Framing: Three-quarter portrait framing from the head to just above the knees, with the scene's hand action readable.
Lens / perspective: 50mm-equivalent natural perspective with balanced proportions and modest depth compression.
Expression: lidded half-open eyes looking away, slack mouth, brows flat and unengaged
overall_intensity: strong — maximal styling presence within the scene; retain chosen exposure and anatomy
skin_exposure: bold — more scene-appropriate shoulder, back, midriff or leg exposure; cover chest and pelvis
action_level: mostly posed — a paused or held moment of the selected activity
source_influence: balanced — her game shows as one accessory and one object in the scene; the outfit keeps its own colours and patterns
separates_preference: prefer separates — prefer separate top and bottom unless the chosen Outfit names a one-piece garment, which wins

WARDROBE: change her clothes completely. From the attached image take only her face, hair and body — not its garment, layers, sash, tassels, jewelry, hair ornaments or background. Dress her exactly as SCENE describes; that outfit must read at first glance, keeping its own recognisable colours and parts. Do not carry the attached image's palette, patterns or trim into the outfit; her game belongs in accessories and props, never in the clothes — never restyle the chosen outfit into her own costume, genre or palette.

ANGLE: the attached image fixes who she is, not how she is posed or shot. Do not copy its head angle, head tilt, gaze direction, face size in frame, camera height or crop — turn her head, set her gaze and place the camera as SCENE describes, and let her face read naturally from that new angle (profile, three-quarter, looking down or away), with her features staying the same.

LOOK-BACK: her back is toward the camera, so her head turns at most a quarter turn over one shoulder — the face shows in profile or three-quarter view, never full-front on a back-facing torso. Her chin sits just above the near shoulder, the far eye and cheek may be partly hidden, the side of the neck shows the turn and the shoulder line continues behind the head; her eyes, not her whole face, swing toward the camera.

ONE MAIN FIGURE: she is the only character in focus. Where the place is busy, other people may appear only as small, soft-focus background extras — never posed with her and never a character from her game. No text, no lettering, no logo, no watermark, no speech bubble, no frame border, no game interface or score.

ANATOMY: natural adult proportions, about 7.5 heads tall — height from the legs, never a smaller head or a longer neck. The neck is a natural length and the head sits close to the shoulders. No body-part enlargement, no extra limbs.

BODY: a normal human body — one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; elbows, knees and wrists bend the human way. Hands and feet may be partly hidden by the pose, what she holds or the frame.

HANDS: natural human hands.

HAND TASK: her hands act naturally for the pose and scene; any idle hand rests in a relaxed, anatomically plausible position. Natural occlusion is allowed; do not force every hand or finger into view.

FINAL CHECK: glossy Korean mobile-game rendering with selective highlights; an original costume — no character, logo, title lettering or interface from the game.
